items.description: arXiv:2611.10110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. items.description: arXiv:2611.10168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Independent verification organizations (IVOs) have emerged as a popular, bipartisan solution for facilitating high-quality independent evaluations of AI technologies. But momentum is outpacing design: there is emerging consensus on the necessary operating conditions for robust IVOs, but little discourse on institutional and policy specifications to ensure those conditions are met. IVOs are currently envisioned primarily as a mechanism operating at the AI frontier and model level to evaluate catastrophic risks. items.description: arXiv:2611.10193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. This constraint is mitigated by expert offloading, which stores part of the model's weight in host memory and executes on demand. Though MoE architecture has computation sparsity, more GPUs are needed for serving increasingly larger frontier models. items.title: ProofDiff: Auditable Argument-Level Comparison of AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs
items.description: arXiv:2611.10233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical understanding depends on the route from hypotheses to conclusion: how the parts of a proof function and which dependencies carry the argument forward. This structure can persist when wording or notation changes, while a small alteration to a hypothesis or inference can produce a different argument beneath similar prose. Formal verification can establish that a rewrite proves the same theorem, but not whether it follows the same mathematical route. Comparing informal proofs, especially those produced or revised by generative models, therefore requires reconstructing which claims, dependencies, and reasoning steps are preserved, reorganized, or replaced. We present ProofDiff, a system for comparing informal mathematical documents.

items.description: arXiv:2611.10265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used to support decisions that require moral consideration. items.description: arXiv:2611.12393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM agents become more autonomous, they are increasingly expected to run as always-on assistants on a user's behalf, identifying work to be done and completing it without being asked. Yet existing benchmarks usually give the agent its task, whereas in knowledge work the requests sit in the user's workspace and the agent must first recognise which obligations exist. items.description: arXiv:2611.12478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Answer accuracy alone does not distinguish failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application. AuDiR (Audio Diagnostic Reasoning) examines these distinctions through controlled input interventions. Each item contains an audio clip, a multiple-choice question, a task-general rule, and a textual description of the acoustic observations needed to answer. Three conditions progressively supply the rule and observations; a fourth removes the audio while retaining the question and rule. items.title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
items.description: arXiv:2611.12552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose SciMARS, a framework for recursive task-local adaptation of multi-agent harnesses in closed-loop scientific discovery. Multi-agent systems coordinate analysis, experimental design, and verification as scientific evidence evolves. However, two problems limit their effectiveness: (i) without shared memory, agents lose observations and repeat work; (ii) fixed role procedures, handoffs, and memory policies perpetuate mistakes despite retained evidence. We address these problems with a shared evidence graph and separate component editors. SciMARS adapts roles and coordination; SciMARS + Memory adds a third editor for how agents record, retrieve, and receive evidence. Candidate probes guide composition and selection of the next harness.

items.description: arXiv:2611.12635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Urban traffic flow prediction is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, yet accurate forecasting under adverse weather conditions remains a significant challenge. items.description: arXiv:2611.12640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI is used in much of the clinical trial pipeline. LLMs appear to be a natural fit given their strengths in biomedical knowledge and statistical reasoning. items.description: arXiv:2611.12675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpretability tools are usually built for one model at a time: a refusal direction, a truthfulness probe, or a steering vector is found with labeled data inside the model it explains. items.description: arXiv:2611.12762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired architecture that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide what to investigate next and how to investigate it. items.description: arXiv:2611.12865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. items.description: arXiv:2603.10967v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models (FMs) show great promise for robust downstream performance across medical imaging tasks and modalities, including cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), following task-specific adaptation. items.description: arXiv:2611.09917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic AI systems are increasingly embedded in scientific workflows, including literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, tool use, writing, and peer review. items.description: arXiv:2611.09919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for subjective tasks such as seeking advice, where there is often no single correct answer. items.description: arXiv:2611.09922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Human-Interactive Robot Learning (HIRL), human teachers assess learning progress by observing agent behavior. items.description: arXiv:2611.09936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Natural language inference (NLI) is a fundamental task of natural language processing and crucial for evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of AI methods. Research has mostly focused on encoder or encoder-decoder architectures. However, the field of decoder-only Large Language Models (LLMs) remains underexplored. items.description: arXiv:2611.09977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models are widely used as synthetic respondents in surveys, behavioral experiments, and market research. items.description: arXiv:2611.10450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model editing provides an efficient way to update factual knowledge in transformer models. Recent approaches reverse edits by modifying, masking, or decomposing model weights, but make recovery dependent on weight-space interventions. We instead show that pre-edit knowledge can be recovered through input-space interventions alone, without modifying the edited model's weights. items.title: Beyond Discrete Ancestry Groups: Distribution-Aware In-Context Learning for Cancer Outcome Prediction Across the Genetic Ancestry Continuum
items.description: arXiv:2611.10464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning models for omics-based prediction of cancer outcomes are commonly built on aggregated data without distinguishing ancestry groups, or under an ancestry-discrete design, which partitions samples into ancestry groups and fits a separate model within each group. Recent evidence shows that this approach is inherently limited: predictive accuracy declines with genetic distance from the training samples, even within a single ancestry group, because the data distribution shifts continuously rather than only between predefined categories. items.title: Hibana: Fast Agentic Inference on Unified-Memory Devices
items.description: arXiv:2611.10469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local AI promises capable personal assistants that run on users' own devices, keeping data and computation under their control. Open-weight models that fit on local devices can now handle practical tasks such as coding. Yet current inference engines fall short. Popular engines such as vLLM and SGLang target datacenter GPUs with dedicated host memory, while local engines underuse the memory hierarchy of unified-memory devices. We present Hibana, an inference engine for unified-memory devices that co-optimizes model representation, memory management, and decoding strategy. Model surgery, the process of editing a trained model's architecture to suit its hardware, changes how the model computes, shrinking its memory footprint and data movement.

items.description: arXiv:2611.10486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, where decisions about which tokens to commit or remask strongly affect output quality. items.title: Safer for Whom? A Systematic Exploration of AI Safety in Eating Disorder Interactions
items.description: arXiv:2611.10488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI assistants advise users about diet, exercise, and weight loss---areas in which unsafe guidance can worsen body dissatisfaction, dietary restriction, compulsive exercise, and other behaviors associated with eating disorders (EDs). items.description: arXiv:2611.10508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as synthetic participants in social, behavioural, and decision-making research, yet it remains unclear whether they can express graded cognitive diversity as assigned when engaging in simulated behaviour. items.description: arXiv:2611.10541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-turn revision often asks a model to replace an earlier organizing frame while preserving still-valid facts and artifact requirements. items.description: arXiv:2611.10542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly improve themselves through self-evolution, distilling execution experience into persistent, reusable skills. items.description: arXiv:2611.10544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical models often report good accuracy on image tasks, but it is rarely clear whether the quantum part is responsible. items.title: Large Language Models without QK-Normalization
items.description: arXiv:2611.10560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm) is widely adopted in modern large language models to control the growth of attention logits and improve training stability. The query norm controls the sharpness of the attention distribution, while the key norm determines how strongly a token attracts different queries. items.description: arXiv:2611.10565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational models of cognition have traditionally relied on abstract symbolic inputs that approximate sensory experiences with simplified vector representations. items.description: arXiv:2611.10592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can generate motion graphics from static images and natural language requests, but it remains difficult to evaluate how well models can follow requests that combine spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements. items.description: arXiv:2611.10599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI can expand cultural collections into prompt-responsive visual media, but historical artworks rarely provide the paired descriptions needed to adapt modern image generators. items.description: arXiv:2611.10601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to process medical records for healthcare tasks such as clinical documentation. items.description: arXiv:2611.10620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Activation probes look like near-perfect monitors for secret collusion among large language model (LLM) agents. items.description: arXiv:2611.10633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantified Boolean formula (QBF), the quantified version of Boolean satisfiability (SAT), is a fundamental problem in constraint solving. items.description: arXiv:2611.10694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. items.description: arXiv:2611.10721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies safeguard industrial processes against catastrophic accidents.
